items.title: William Russell Interview, 1976-02-16
items.q: Ewing Nunn, who's probably the most, I don't know what you'd say, the most engineer of anybody I know, a wonderful engineer.

ctx.x: American Music got started and how that relates to Bunk Johnson being well known. Or did that help his cause? Yeah, we might talk a little about that.

The reason I got into the business at all was partly due to these first records I mentioned, the Jazzmen, that were so badly recorded on the little machine. About a $200 list price machine it was, a federal recorder. Some kid that worked, he was a teenage kid, I guess, that worked for Grunewald's. Happened to have it. He's the only one we could find that had any blanks around that would be able to record the band in 1942 when Dave issued the records. And those records were so bad that I'll tell you one story that…

He hadn't thrown them out fortunately, but he probably would have very soon if Dave hadn't gotten back. He could have thrown them in a wastebasket. So he thought it was just a joke, you know, that he sent something to amuse him. So Dave said, no, that's the real thing. It had to be worked on and issued. So anyway, I decided after that that I couldn't do much worse. So I got a machine. My machine only cost about $40. My brother put a little secondhand machine together and then bought an amplifier.
